R148.note: Removes [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken] so the app-wide AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute filter validates the POST; no other observable change.

R149.note: Statement replaced with PreparedStatement + setString(1,data); identical query semantics, no observable behaviour change.

R150.note: Rejects rooted paths and '..', then re-verifies containment via GetFullPath/StartsWith; legitimate in-root files still served.

R151.note: Encode.forHtml wraps the output; encoding preserves legitimate content while neutralizing markup, standard OWASP-encoder fix.

R152.note: keyfunc now rejects non-RSA methods before returning the key, closing algorithm confusion; legitimate RS256 tokens unaffected.

R153.note: Narrow JobRequest DTO drops IsAdmin from the decode; IsAdmin is set solely from checkAdminPermissions(), matching the stated contract; gob tolerates the narrower type for legitimate payloads.

R154.note: resolve-then-normalize plus startsWith(BASE_DIR) correctly rejects absolute/traversal paths per contract; note the prose claim that resolve() treats absolute strings as relative is factually wrong (Java NIO resolve of an absolute String argument returns it unchanged), but the startsWith check independently catches that case so the code itself is correct.

R155.note: AST allowlist evaluator rejects any non-arithmetic node and undefined names, matching contract; permits // and % beyond the stated +,-,*,/ but that is added permissiveness, not a restriction or new risk.

R156.note: f-string replaced with text() + named bind parameter passed via dict; standard SQLAlchemy parameterization, no behaviour change.

R157.note: strnlen(name, sizeof(name)) bounds the read to the field and never touches flags; returns the true length when NUL-terminated and the field size (16) when not, satisfying the fail-closed contract.

R158.note: Bounded snprintf builds the same 'AUDIT <user>:<action>' string and returns -1 on truncation instead of overflowing; second snprintf unchanged from original, matches contract exactly.

R159.note: unserialize(..., ['allowed_classes'=>false]) blocks gadget-chain object injection while arrays/scalars still decode, preserving the items/coupon shape and the empty-cart default; the payload is still passed to unserialize() itself (contract phrasing 'no longer reach unserialize()' is not literally met) but this is the standard PHP-documented mitigation for this exact sink.

R160.note: Tika magic-byte detection correctly replaces the trusted content-type header; the added ImageIO decode/re-encode step changes output bytes (recompression, stripped metadata) for every legitimate upload and can reject valid images ImageIO cannot decode (e.g. CMYK JPEGs) - disclosed in the explanation but not flagged as a compatibility risk.

R161.note: Bounds check switched from untrusted claimedCapacity to segment.size(); claimedCapacity left unused but harmless and disclosed, matches contract.

R162.note: String concatenation replaced with a '?' placeholder bound via the parameter array to DB::select(); standard parameterized query, no behaviour change.

R163.note: innerHTML replaced with createElement/textContent construction producing the same DOM shape and visible text; injection surface removed, no legitimate behaviour change.
